summary.text: Pamela J. Hunter is the incumbent Democratic and Working Families Party candidate for New York State Assembly District 128 in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A U.S. Army veteran and former Syracuse Common Council member, she was first elected to the Assembly in 2015 and serves as Speaker Pro Tempore.

paragraphs.text: Hunter grew up in Upstate New York and is an honorably discharged U.S. Army veteran.

She earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from Strayer College in Washington, D.C., holds a professional certification in human resources, and received an honorary Doctor of Humane Letters from Le Moyne College.

Her official biography says she held executive positions with nonprofit organizations and professional service firms, and served on boards including AccessCNY, Catholic Charities, Meals on Wheels and the Syracuse Industrial Development Agency.
Hunter served three years on the Syracuse Common Council, where she chaired the Public Safety Committee, before her election to the Assembly in 2015.
She represents the 128th Assembly District, which covers parts of the City of Syracuse and the towns of Dewitt, Onondaga and Salina, and chairs the Subcommittee on Women Veterans.
She is a member of the Insurance, Rules, Veterans' Affairs, and Ways and Means committees.
She is also the immediate past president of the National Council of Insurance Legislators, according to her official biography.
